rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm this rule guards: a reader hits a noun/pronoun with nothing to hang it on. Closest candidates are chunk 0's 'M5 worktree' / 'the re-send' (line 7) and chunk 1's 'the m5/<slug> branch' / 'protected Run coordinates block' (line 19-20) -- all cross-module. Checked against arc-earned carve-out: M5's own module file is literally titled 'Learn from the test, re-send packaged' (curriculum/trainings/agentic-engineering-101/learn-from-the-test.md:1) and uses 'un-packaged'/'packaged'/'re-send' throughout its own body -- earned there. M6's own module file (curriculum/trainings/agentic-engineering-101/spot-gaps-build-the-loop.md, ## Start here) states 'Open a fresh session in the Module 5 worktree... You walk in holding two sessions... The un-packaged Module 4 send-off. The packaged Module 5 re-send' -- this exercise is the very next link after the module's own Start Here + the-2-frontiers.md opener in module include order, so 'M5 worktree'/'re-send' is prior context per the module-arc-beats carve-out before this exercise's own chunk 0 ever uses it. Within-file referents (line 28 'four-dimension plan summary' -> the four prompt bullets in chunk 1's {{prompt:...}}; line 34 'the diagnosis' -> the diff work just done in chunks 1-2) all resolve to same-file prior chunks. No never-named, no vague-with-history, no stranded-by-rechunk instance found.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every backward reference points at a beat that exists.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm guarded: a callback to a beat that got cut or renamed, stranding the student. This file's only backward-pointing beats are the M4 un-packaged send-off and the M5 packaged re-send (chunk 0/1). Verified both exist and are named identically in M6's own module file (spot-gaps-build-the-loop.md ## Start here: 'The un-packaged Module 4 send-off. The packaged Module 5 re-send.') and in the M5 module title itself. No 'the X you did/saw' phrasing pointing at a beat absent from the current module set.

Harm guarded: a slide that says nothing standalone (bare wait-state or one context-dependent bullet). Each of the 4 ##-chunks carries 2-3 self-carrying bullets plus an instruction line (chunks 1 and 3 also carry the expanded prompt block). None reduces to a lone context-dependent fragment: e.g. chunk 4 (lines 41-45) stands on its own as 'approve if the agent pauses; push back if the cut spreads past one rule.'

Harm guarded: header promises something the chunk body contradicts or never delivers. Checked all 4: 'Diff the two sessions, rank the gaps' (line 17) -- body diffs (line 22) and the expanded prompt ends 'which gap matters most? Rank by damage-to-a-future-session' -- both halves land. 'Read the contrast, push back where it generalises' (line 26) -- three bullets on exactly that. 'Cut one stale rule the diagnosis killed' (line 32) -- body motivates the cut then instructs 'Ask Claude to cut the one rule the diagnosis killed' (line 37). 'Say go, unless the cut spreads past the one rule' (line 41) -- bullets cover both the approve case and the pushback case. No header outruns its body.

Checked all sub-items across all 4 chunks plus both expanded prompt bodies: no 'Not X. Not Y. Z.' construction; no anaphora/epistrophe triples; no number-with-retraction; no abstraction-noun stacks; no empty-leg verb triplets. Closest candidate for self-grading superlative is line 13 '**The point:** two sessions are enough to place every lesson' -- stays inside because it is a world/method claim ('two sessions suffice diagnostically'), not a training-value claim ('one of the most useful moves in the training'); it does not grade the exercise's own worth. No sub-item fires.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Heading grammar is the mood switch, and it is load-bearing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: All four ## headings are imperative/phase-label, matching the exercise-file grammar: 'Diff the two sessions, rank the gaps' (17), 'Read the contrast, push back where it generalises' (26), 'Cut one stale rule the diagnosis killed' (32), 'Say go, unless the cut spreads past the one rule' (41). None is a declarative law-statement wearing an exercise heading, none is a claim-shaped header that should be a bullet instead.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A bullet earns its slot or dies -- three classes that read as rigour and carry nothing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Checked all body bullets (lines 19-20, 28-30, 34-35, 43-44) against the three classes. None is doctrine restatement (no lens/law re-announced a second time in this file), none is self-referential design commentary (no 'you are inside a pedagogy' framing -- bullets describe the student's own artefacts, not the curriculum's design), none is an aphorism kicker restating its own header or the point line. Closest pair: line 34 (concrete diagnostic result: this two-session test surfaced bad rules) and line 35 (the general half-life principle) sit adjacent but carry different content -- one is what happened, the other is the retained take-home the Leap test names ('cuts a stale rule ... instead of letting the rules-file rot') -- not a restatement of the same move.
